topics.title: Coursework
topics.summary: The retained student record supports effective, ethical, critical and transparent AI use generally. That support does not establish permission for a particular assessment; old scenario rules remain excluded.
topics.scope: General student support, IT guidance and PGR/research advice have different scopes. Old Regulation32 and three-scenario records are excluded; new2026–27 proposals are pending, so no current exam permission is inferred.

claims.text: University of Glasgow student guidance says the university does not seek to prohibit student AI-tool use generally and instead supports effective, ethical, critical, and transparent use.

evidence.quote: Consequently, rather than seek to prohibit your use of these tools, we want to support you in learning how to use them effectively, ethically, critically, and transparently.
evidence.title: University of Glasgow - Artificial Intelligence - Info for Students
evidence.location: What is the University of Glasgow's position on AI?

topics.title: Disclosure
topics.summary: The student record says unacknowledged AI or computational help in university work counts as misconduct. Acknowledgement is necessary context, not blanket permission to use AI.

claims.text: University of Glasgow student guidance says using AI or other computational aids in university work without acknowledging the input counts as academic misconduct.

evidence.quote: It is important to note that using any form of AI or other computational aids in your university coursework, study, exams, or research without acknowledging that input counts as academic misconduct.
evidence.title: University of Glasgow - Artificial Intelligence - Info for Students

topics.title: Privacy and data
topics.summary: IT guidance says confidential or sensitive university or third-party information should not enter AI tools. The PGR checklist separately cautions against research data and peer-review material.
topics.scope: General student support, IT guidance and PGR/research advice have different scopes. Old Regulation32 and three-scenario records are excluded; new2026–27 proposals are pending, so no current exam permission is inferred.

claims.text: University of Glasgow IT guidance says confidential or sensitive information belonging to the university or a third party should not be put into AI tools.

evidence.quote: Confidential or sensitive information (including, for example, IP) belonging to the University or any third party should not be put into AI tools.
evidence.title: MyGlasgow - IT - 365 - Copilot - guidance

claims.text: University of Glasgow's PGR GenAI checklist advises PGR students to avoid uploading confidential or sensitive information, including research data and peer review content, to AI tools.

evidence.quote: Avoid uploading confidential or sensitive information to an AI tool (this includes research data and peer review content).

topics.title: Research and publication
topics.summary: Research guidance records critical oversight and relevant ethics/data-protection processes. The PGR checklist has a separate audience; full current-source verification remains incomplete.
topics.scope: General student support, IT guidance and PGR/research advice have different scopes. Old Regulation32 and three-scenario records are excluded; new2026–27 proposals are pending, so no current exam permission is inferred.

claims.text: University of Glasgow researcher guidance states that any use of generative AI tools by staff, students, and researchers must be accompanied by critical analysis and oversight by the user.

evidence.quote: There is therefore one overriding principle, which applies to all staff, students, and researchers at the University: any use of generative AI tools must be accompanied by critical analysis and oversight on the part of the user.
evidence.title: Generative AI Guidance for Researchers - University of Glasgow

claims.text: University of Glasgow researcher guidance says AI tools used as part of research design, methods, disciplinary toolkit, or research subject should be covered by relevant ethical approval and data protection processes.

evidence.quote: Where AI tools form part of your research design or methods, the tool kit within your discipline, or are a subject of your research, your use of them as a researcher should be covered by relevant ethical approval and data protection processes.
evidence.title: Generative AI Guidance for Researchers - University of Glasgow

additionalTopics.title: Teaching guidance
additionalTopics.summary: Assessment-design guidance encourages demonstrating skills beyond recall and says AI use is not always plagiarism. It does not remove assessment-specific restrictions or approve a new scenario policy.
additionalTopics.scope: General student support, IT guidance and PGR/research advice have different scopes. Old Regulation32 and three-scenario records are excluded; new2026–27 proposals are pending, so no current exam permission is inferred.

claims.text: University of Glasgow assessment-design guidance says GenAI use in assessment should not always be treated as plagiarism and encourages assessment design that lets students demonstrate skills beyond knowledge recall.

evidence.quote: It is important to recognise that the use of GenAI in assessment should not, in all cases, be treated as plagiarism. Rather we should carefully consider how we design assessment to ensure that students can demonstrate skills beyond purely knowledge recall.
evidence.title: How can I adapt assessment to deal with GenAI?
